summary: Our project is a space survival game developed using Scratch for living on mars. The game allows players to experience some of the challenges of surviving in space by managing energy resources, making water, planting food, and producing oxygen. The user(player) is going to make choices and it will impact their survival. Users will learn how energy can be used to support long-term space exploration. Our project addresses the challenge by turning complex space science concepts into an interactive game that is easy and fun to understand. It helps players learn how to create living sources in space and how important it is for astronauts and future space missions. This project is important because energy, food, water, and oxygen is the key to the challenges of living beyond Earth. Through our game, we hope to inspire more people to explore space science and understand the technology needed to make future space exploration possible.
details:
This interactive game is designed around a lunar survival scenario in which a character must stay alive on the Moon. The player begins with a set of interconnected, essential resources: water generated using rocket fuel, oxygen extracted from that water supply, food harvested from a lunar farm, and electricity powered by solar panels. By managing these delicate systems, the game encourages players to think critically, stay open-minded, and spark their curiosity about the real-world challenges of space exploration and off-world survival.

To build the project, our team first mapped out all the core resources required for survival and researched the best methods to maintain a steady, balanced supply. Once our game mechanics were planned, we used Scratch to code the interactive logic and brought the lunar environment to life using a combination of custom hand-drawn artwork and curated images from the web.
